claims.text: Think thru the six Ws: wound infect, H2O (UTI), wind (atelectasis, PNA), walking (DVT), wonder drugs, widgets (devices, drains).
claims.quote: Common causes of fever during the days or weeks after surgery include the so-called "six Ws": Wound infections Water (eg, UTIs) Wind (eg, atelectasis, pneumonia) Walking (eg, DVTs) Wonder drugs (eg, drug-induced fever) Widgets (eg, implantable devices, drains)

claims.text: Poss sepsis: urine and blood cultures, CXR, lytes, glucose, BUN, creatinine, lactate and liver enzymes.
claims.quote: Patients with red flag findings suggesting sepsis require cultures (urine and blood), chest radiograph, and evaluation for metabolic abnormalities with measurement of serum electrolytes, glucose, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, lactate, and liver enzymes.

claims.text: Wound w signs of infect: exploration and drainage of any abscess.
claims.quote: If they occur, wound exploration and drainage of abscesses, systemic antibiotics, or both may be required.

claims.text: Pleural effusion ≥ 10 mm that = new or of uncertain cause: thoracentesis.
claims.quote: Thoracentesis should be performed in almost all patients who have pleural fluid that is ≥ 10 mm in thickness on CT, ultrasound, or lateral decubitus radiograph and that is new or of uncertain etiology.
Thoracentesis should be performed using ultrasonographic guidance in all cases, to improve procedural success and reduce complications
Identify purulent effusions strongly suggestive of empyema

claims.text: Pleural fluid: total protein, glucose, LDH, cell count w differential and Gram stain; pH and cultures when indicated.
claims.quote: Fluid should always be sent for total protein, glucose, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), cell count and cell differential, and Gram stain. Other tests such as pleural fluid pH, aerobic and anaerobic bacterial cultures, cytology, tuberculosis fluid markers [adenosine deaminase or interferon-gamma], amylase, mycobacterial and fungal stains and cultures, triglycerides, and cholesterol are used in appropriate clinical settings.
